issues.issue: Must a PRRA officer consider the interests of a Canadian-born child when assessing the risk of removing a parent?
issues.applicant_position: Officer has no such duty; child-interest review belongs to the s.25(1) H&C process.
issues.respondent_position: Officer must consider the interests of Canadian-born children; the Applications Judge so held.
issues.result_quote: A PRRA officer has no obligation to consider, in the context of the PRRA, the interests of a Canadian-born child

issues.issue: Did the officer have to consider a greater risk to the parents if the children went to Hungary, when this was not raised with the officer?
issues.applicant_position: Officer was not at fault; the submission was not made to the officer.
issues.respondent_position: Officer should have considered the parents' greater risk of persecution if the children went to Hungary.
issues.result_quote: since counsel did not make this submission to the officer, he cannot complain that the officer was at fault in not considering it.

issues.issue: Must a PRRA officer assess the most serious risks because the s.25(1) H&C remedy may come too late?
issues.applicant_position: Serious risks belong to the H&C process; a removals officer can defer removal to consider them.
issues.respondent_position: PRRA officer must consider the most serious risks because the s.25(1) remedy is illusory.
issues.result_quote: although the respondents were not entitled to have this issue taken into account by the PRRA officer
